subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class pre-threshold compaction warnings, a structured handoff/checkpoint turn, and bounded agent-requested compaction deferral to core, or keep current memoryFlush/notifyUser/checkpoint behavior as the supported lifecycle?
rationale: The request changes compaction timing, persisted session semantics, public config, and authority handling across compaction boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product/security contract safely.

options.title: Design Core Lifecycle
options.body: Define the warning thresholds, handoff checkpoint schema, deferral authorization rules, and upgrade path before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Notices Only
options.body: Limit core work to user/agent-visible warning improvements and leave deferral/checkpoint authority out of scope for now.

options.title: Decline New Core Surface
options.body: Keep the existing memoryFlush, compaction hooks, notifyUser, and checkpoint metadata as the supported model.

recommendation.title: Design Core Lifecycle
recommendation.body: Define the warning thresholds, handoff checkpoint schema, deferral authorization rules, and upgrade path before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the closest existing pre-compaction memoryFlush behavior and is the strongest available routing candidate for the lifecycle/product decision.
